resources.string: Use Android\'s built-in effects instead of recording the sound
No recording permission, and it works with apps that block recording. Only the equalizers, bass, compressor and limiter work. May not work on every phone.
This phone does not offer the built-in effect global mode needs

Normally this app records what your phone plays, changes it, and plays it back. That needs the screen recording permission, and some apps (Spotify, for one) refuse to be recorded.

Global mode does not record anything. It sets up Android's own sound effect, the one music players use for their equalizers, and fills it with your settings. So it works with every app, with no recording prompt.

The catch: Android's effect can only do equalizing, a compressor and a limiter. The Multiband, Graphic (including AutoEq and Match EQ) and Parametric EQ, Bass boost, FET compressor, Maximiser, Output control and Balance carry over. Every other card is greyed out while global mode is on, and keeps its settings for when you switch back.

It adds a small delay (about 40 ms) and some phones handle it better than others. The check screen shows what Android did with it.

All sound covers whatever plays through the phone\'s main music output, including apps that never say they are playing. Each app separately only reaches apps that announce themselves to equalizers (Poweramp, Neutron, Musicolet, VLC and others) or that the app spots while they play, but suits phones where All sound does nothing.
